concerns.text: FR-002 still reads 'scaffold-based split with [deferred] of the data allocated to training and [deferred] each to validation and test sets'. FR-013 and Constitution Principle VI both mandate a fixed 80/10/10 split; the placeholder directly contradicts them and leaves the split ratios unmeasurable. Restore explicit 80/10/10. (Prior concern, unresolved.)

Scenario 3 still says 'selected as one of the top [deferred] highest FQY values of the test set'. The placeholder prevents reproducible instantiation of the test input and is inconsistent with the spec's own rule that only empirical measurements are deferred, not selection rules. Replace with a concrete rule (e.g., top-5% or fixed top-N). (Prior concern, unresolved.)

Two different interpretability pass thresholds coexist without reconciliation: US-3 Scenario 3 requires 'at least 3 of the top 5 substructures' to match reference motifs for a single high-FQY molecule, while SC-005 requires '≥60% overlap (at least 12 of the 20 substructures)' on the top-20 aggregate. State explicitly that these are distinct checks (per-molecule spot check vs aggregate enrichment) or unify them; as written a reader cannot tell which governs pass/fail.
FR-003 says '≤5 million parameters' while the Assumptions section says 'a GNN with <5 M parameters'. Minor boundary-condition mismatch (≤ vs <); align wording.

FR-002 still reads 'scaffold-based split with [deferred] of the data allocated to training and [deferred] each to validation and test sets'. The 80/10/10 ratio is a constitution-mandated constant (Principle VI), not an empirical value to defer, and FR-013 already asserts 80/10/10 — the placeholder makes the split ratios unmeasurable and the spec internally inconsistent. Restore explicit 80/10/10. Previously raised, unresolved.

Scenario 3 still says 'selected as one of the top [deferred] highest FQY values of the test set'. The placeholder prevents reproducible instantiation of the test input. Replace with a concrete selection rule (e.g., top-5% highest FQY values, or top-N with N fixed). Previously raised, unresolved.

Scenario 3 still says 'selected as one of the top [deferred] highest FQY values of the test set'. The placeholder prevents reproducible instantiation of the test input. Replace with a concrete selection rule (e.g., top-5% highest FQY values, or top-N with N fixed). Previously raised, unresolved.

SC-001 says GNN R² "measured against the linear regression baseline and must be ≥ 0.7 to demonstrate a meaningful improvement", but the pass condition is absolute (GNN R² ≥ 0.7), not relative. If the ECFP4 baseline also reaches R² ≥ 0.7, the GNN passes while demonstrating NO improvement over fingerprints — the core hypothesis (graph topology beats fingerprints) is never actually tested. Add an explicit relative criterion (e.g., GNN R² exceeds baseline R² by a stated margin, or a paired test on per-molecule errors).

The interpretability validation risks near-tautology. FR-006 defines substructures BY CONSTRUCTION as "contiguous aromatic or conjugated fragments", and the reference set (FR-016) is fluorophore motifs, which are themselves overwhelmingly aromatic/conjugated. High overlap between top-attribution aromatic fragments and an aromatic motif catalog is substantially guaranteed by the aggregation rule, independent of what the model learned. To make SC-005 an empirical finding, compare against a null (e.g., overlap of randomly selected conjugated fragments, or attributions from an untrained/shuffled model) or include non-conjugated fragments in the ranking pool.
